source_review.notes: Checked the primary Borg, Omega, Mesos, DRF, and Firmament publications plus current Apache Hadoop, Kubernetes, Linux kernel, and NVIDIA documentation. All thirteen final cited URLs returned HTTP 200. Architecture-specific behavior is attributed and separated from the generic vector-feasibility model.

evidence: Reviewed dimensions D; physical C, reservation S, headroom H, unavailable U, allocatable A, request r, limit l, use u, placement P, total R, allocation x, and dominant share s.
Checked CPU, GiB, device counts, rates, capacities, fractions, and time-dependent usage retain explicit units and scopes.
Checked request, limit, allocation, usage, work, rate, and outcome are not conflated.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Vector quantities are componentwise and node-scoped unless cluster totals are explicitly introduced.

evidence: Executed multiresource-fragmentation with Python 3.14.4 and reproduced free vectors (2,12)/(6,4), aggregate (8,16), no fit for (4,8), and fragmentation true.
Recomputed 64-6-4-2 = 52 GiB allocatable memory and request/limit burst totals of 4/8 CPU.
Recomputed dominant shares 0.40/0.40 in Example 7.
Recomputed Exercise 1 as 28 CPU/92 GiB allocatable with 27 CPU/96 GiB demand, and Exercise 3 dominant shares 0.30/0.30.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Examples are deterministic scalar illustrations and do not estimate stochastic performance or topology feasibility.

evidence: Verified allocatable capacity is physical minus reservations, headroom, and unavailable capacity componentwise.
Checked per-node componentwise request sums are necessary for scalar fit.
Verified aggregate cluster fit is insufficient by constructive fragmented placement.
Checked dominant share is the maximum per-dimension allocation fraction under a consistent cluster capacity vector.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Scalar feasibility is explicitly not claimed sufficient for device, topology, policy, gang, duration, or performance constraints.

evidence: Reviewed zero/full capacity, rounding, giant tasks, complementary and identical shapes, indivisible devices, ports, topology, gangs, and volume attachment.
Reviewed startup, steady, shuffle, checkpoint, restore, compaction, reclaim delay, and simultaneous tenant peaks.
Reviewed under/overrequest, missing request, request/limit mismatch, CPU throttle, memory OOM, disk-full/IO saturation, and device failure.
Reviewed stale/forged inventory, tenant inflation, label misuse, double allocation, cross-tenant device exposure, and model migration.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Admission safety, isolation, fairness, liveness, placement quality, performance, security, and recoverability remain distinct.

evidence: Traced physical capacity through system reservation, headroom, unavailable inventory, allocatable reporting, atomic allocation, free capacity, and runtime use.
Checked every promised dimension has canonical units, measurement, freshness, accounting, enforcement, and failure behavior.
Checked node vector fit precedes identity/topology/affinity/security/storage/gang predicates.
Checked overcommit and reclaim preserve protected classes through explicit throttle/evict order and recovery headroom.
invariant_checking.notes: Overhead is assigned once to node reservation or workload request to prevent both omission and double subtraction.

evidence: Reviewed the ten-step audit from workload promise and inventory through resource classification, fit, time, overcommit, fairness, reconciliation, and validation.
Checked componentwise inequality proof assumes current inventory, atomic allocation, canonical units, and node granularity.
Checked fragmentation counterexample proves aggregate capacity cannot replace placement feasibility.
Checked request-based admission is not presented as proof of runtime performance or truthful declarations.
proof_review.notes: Generic resource theory is separated from Borg, Omega, Mesos, Hadoop, Kubernetes, Linux, and NVIDIA implementations.

evidence: Audited feasible, allocatable, reserved, unavailable, guaranteed, reclaimable, overcommitted, fragmented, fair, isolated, and enforced.
Confirmed necessary scalar fit is not labeled sufficient placement or performance.
Confirmed dominant-resource fairness is scoped to its assumptions and not labeled a complete production scheduler.
Confirmed labels, limits, usage samples, aggregate headroom, and high utilization are not mislabeled as reservations or safety proofs.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Claims name the resource dimension, topology, time scale, workload class, and enforcement scope where material.

evidence: Reviewed request/allocation/use, fit failures, pending reasons, fragmentation, inventory age, throttling, pressure, eviction/OOM, device error, and workload outcomes.
Confirmed no universal headroom, overcommit factor, request percentile, resource weight, reclaim deadline, or utilization target is prescribed.
Confirmed the executable fixture is not production evidence for scheduler quality, concurrency, topology, fairness, or enforcement.
Confirmed production changes require correlated traces, adversarial mixtures, failure/recovery, canary pools, accounting reconciliation, and rollback evidence.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Measurement recommendations preserve workload phase, concurrency, correlation, software version, and stable resource units.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed resource taxonomy, allocatable construction, request/limit/use separation, vector fit, fragmentation, heterogeneity, devices/topology, storage/network, overhead, time, overcommit/QoS, fairness, scheduler architecture, calibration, observability, and evolution.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed implementable inventory, workload APIs, admission predicates, device claims, phase sizing, system overhead, stale health, QoS/reclaim, trace replay, accounting dashboards, canary migration, and rollback. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from capacity vectors and semantic resource types through placement and operations. Ten examples and five answered exercises cover allocatable math, request/limit/use, fragmentation, devices, I/O, recovery, DRF, reclaim, stale inventory, executable fit, and production review.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external Borg/Omega/Mesos/Hadoop/Kubernetes/Linux/NVIDIA maintainer, scheduler/resource-allocation researcher, hardware/device/network/storage engineer, SRE/capacity/FinOps/security specialist, accessibility specialist, or certification review is claimed.
